July 2009 # Double trouble - The acute phase of the financial crisis appears to be over. Improved economic sentiment has pushed LME prices to a new annual high over the past month, despite SHFE prices having fallen from their early April highs. - There has been little to report on the mine side, as prices above $4,500/t mean that there is no reason for miners to cut back. Sulphuric acid remains an issue for smelters, but has yet to lead to more cutbacks. - Copper prices on the LME have been driven by sentiment over the last couple of months. However, this sentiment is likely to face significant headwinds. Demand growth remains anaemic and Chinese imports should ease back, allowing LME stocks to rise, placing downward pressure on prices. As sentiment weakens, the dollar’s safe haven status could see its value strengthen and force prices even lower. |The supply/demand

In the near term, we expect that economic developments will drive copper price movements, as was t

he case in Q4 last year. Chinese demand (bolstered by low scrap availability) provided a sound fundamental basis for the rise in copper prices through April this year. The relief that we are likely to avert Great Depression 2.0, on the back of massive government support for the global financial system, has been joined in the past couple of months by hopes that an economic recovery is imminent and an appetite for risk has returned. This has fuelled a rally across many asset classes, which has seen copper prices reach new highs for the year. We support the view that the next Great Depression has been averted, yet we remain cautious on calling the end of the economic downturn, let alone that a wider economic recovery is just round the corner. Until April, copper prices on the LME were pulled higher by movements on SHFE, but SHFE prices have since declined while prices on the LME have continued to trade higher. The onset of the financial fallout in Q4 2008 saw several billion dollars of investments cashed in. Some of this money is now seeking to jump onto the “recovery” bandwagon that has seen copper rise by 90.8% and oil by more than 100% from their low points in December, while the Dow Jones Industrial average is up by 37% since its late March low for the year. In talking to the financial community, they report that their clients remain very bullish about copper and commodities in general. We attribute this largely due to the fear of missing out on recent gains. As the chart to the right shows, open interest on the LME rose along with prices over the past month, which indicates a build in fresh long positions. ## **Prices top out…** Long build up followed by

The rise in copper prices has seen the 6-month upward trend in copper being tested. 3-month LME prices hit a new 2009 high of $5,381/t on 11th June, but then fell to $4,690/t by 23rd June. From a fundamental perspective, the market is moving into a seasonally slower period of demand, due to the northern hemisphere summer. Meanwhile, the rate of decline in LME inventory is slowing and stocks are likely to rise in the coming months, as fresh Chinese buying activity diminishes and demand elsewhere in the world will not be able to soak up surplus cathode. Chinese buying activity is likely to remain subdued throughout Q3, as signs of oversupply in the country continue to mount. SHFE stocks rose sharply to 68,536t on 18th June, their highest level since 23rd August 2007 and prices on SHFE are currently down by 10% from their early April highs. Some interpreted Chinese cathode imports ris

ing to a new all-time high of 337,320t in May as bullish news.  However, given the shipping times to move material across to the country, we see this as a lagging indicator of the strength of Chinese demand and May is likely to have been the high water mark for cathode imports this year. 

The open interest chart above provides some indication that the copper market may be questioning the strength of copper’s Q2 rally, as both open interest and prices fell from their mid-June highs, indicating long liquidation.  This could reflect some players locking in short term profits or others pulling out, having been spooked by the re-emergence of worries about the economic underpinnings for copper demand. 

## **…but has the economy bottomed out?** 

The current economic downturn is still tracking the early phases of the Great Depression in terms of industrial production, while the declines in trade and stock markets are ahead of the descent seen 80 years

ago.  Of course, there were trade tensions and monetary policy failings that exacerbated the crisis back then. This time, policy makers are trying to avoid making matters worse and a 25% slump in GDP is not expected.  However, in a wake up call that helped dampen the bullish sentiment in global markets, the World Bank recently revised down its forecast for world GDP growth in 2009 to a decline of 2.9% from a previous 1.7% fall.  CRU currently forecasts a global decline of 2.5%, led by 6.0% declines in the export dependent German and Japanese economies. 

Financial and economic crises can lead to negative feedback, creating a downward spiral in economic output and metals demand.  In particular, this economic crisis is likely to lead to higher bankruptcies and place further stress on the financial sector.  According to the most pessimistic analysts, the global economy and hence copper consumption faces the possibility of a severe double dip recession, a financially induced downturn in 2008 followed by an economically driven recession in 2009-2010.  For our part, CRU believes demand will remain slow due to extended summer shutdowns. 

## **Demand for spot cathode slows…** 

China has been at the forefront of using stimulus packages to drive the economic recovery.  However, as outlined earlier, there are signs that Chinese copper buying activity has slowed down over the past month. Cathode imports touched a new all-time high, but this headline grabbing statistic has hidden the fact that Chinese imports of copper units across all copper raw material imports (concentrates, anode & blister, scrap and cathode) actually peaked in April.  In addition, it is widely considered that cancelled warrants on the LME have been a good indicator of the amount of material heading to China.  This trade is drying up, as the arbitrage has shrunk and cancelled warrants fell below 15,000t on 24<sup>th</sup> June, whi

ch takes them back to below the average level recorded over the past ten years on a percentage basis. Some support for copper demand in China should come from the success of the scheme introduced by the government to boost purchases by rural households of domestic appliances. The scheme provides a 13% rebate to buyers of selected televisions, refrigerators, washing machines, air conditioners, mobile phones and computers and is being extended on a trial basis to urban households in nine provinces, who will receive a 10% rebate on a trade in of older models. Elsewhere, though, demand remains extremely poor. This month’s Consumption trends delves into North East Asian demand and shows that the restocking seen in Q2 this year appears to be coming to an end, as semis producers have limited visibility regarding future demand. ## **…production continues with few disruptions** There has been little to report on the mine side, and with prices above $4,500/t there is no reason for miners to cut back. Indeed, © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 12 Copper Monitor July 2009 **www.crumonitor.com** miners are taking advantage of these attractive prices to sell forward. The changes in the forward curve structure, which has returned to a broadly flat structure currently, support this view. On the smelting/refining side, Pan Pacific announced that it will maintain its 7% cutback into Q3 in response to easing in Chinese imports. Meanwhile, refined production in China has been rising month-on-month since the seasonal low in January. It was not until May that production began to recover strongly when increased scrap availability allowed restarts and boosted production from secondary sources. The acid situation in China has not yet led to any production cuts, but some Chinese smelters are facing difficulties in off-loading their acid. This, combined with record levels of sulphuric acid imports from Japan and Ko

rea, has seen the Chinese smelting industry instigate an anti-dumping investigation. If this action is successful then any production cuts would more than likely affect the Japanese and/or Korean copper producers. ## **Premiums stabilise** |**Premiums stabilise**

The US premium has also remained unchanged in a range from 4-5.5¢/lb, with the top end of the range only achievable by traders having the right material in the right place for a customer that has been caught short. With the Chinese market oversupplied and the closing of the arbitrage window, the Chinese import premium has fallen steadily over the past month to an average of $80/t in the past week. ## **Mergers & acquisitions back in the lime light** The proposed merger of Xstrata and Anglo American shows that the M&A bandwagon is still rumbling on. The collapse of the Rio Tinto-Chinalco link up in early June was not entirely unexpected, as the recovery in metals prices since the deal was announced made the terms of the tie up generous to Chinalco. However, the success of Minmetals acquisition of OZ Minerals demonstrated that Chinese companies can make inroads into western mining assets (although Prominent Hill was excluded from the deal). In addition, Asarco is at the centre of a bidding war between Vedanta’s Sterlite subsidiary and Grupo Mexico, with each company upping their original bids (see Industry News page 10 for details of the latest moves). The Xstrata-Anglo American merger would create a new No.1 copper mine producer (1.579Mt on a 2008 basis) and the no. 3 copper refiner (1.033Mt on a 2008 basis). Anglo American has rejected the merger, but several large shareholders are pressing for Anglo American management to remain open to the idea of the merger. It is too early to say how this will play out, but an eventually successful bid (and even a counter bid by Anglo) is not beyond the realms of possibility given potential cost savings available. However, demand still remained well down on last year in Japan and Taiwan, and now looks to be softening again as this restocking phase comes to an end. In South Korea, semis production was up year-on-year as wire and cable consumption was boosted by government initiatives: we understand that Korea’s national power utility is spending 68% of its 2009 procurement budget in H1. This means that South Korean demand is likely to soften in H2. In Japan, we do not expect further recovery this year. Domestic demand from the construction, machinery and automotive sectors remains weak. In the export market, Japan is being hit by a strengthening yen, and there are signs of a softening in demand from China and the Middle East. Wire and cable shipments fell by 31% y-o-y in May, to 44,700t, according to the Japanese Electric Wire and Cable Makers’ Association, their lowest level since February 1975. Makers remain pessimistic about the outlook for the rest of the year. The three major Japanese rolled copper makers (Hitachi, Dowa and Nippon) plan to cut their production of flat rolled products in the first half of fiscal 2009 (started April 2009) by 32% y-o-y to 48,186t. Taiwan is also being hit by weakening orders from China, which have slowed down after a strong start to the year. NE Asian semis production recovers,

Thus far, the run down in producer semis inventories seems to have largely kept pace with cutbacks in production, with Taiwanese stocks now having readjusted to match a sharp decline in output late last year. ## **Automotive scrapping schemes boost European car sales** European car sales continued to fall in May, with new car registrations down by 4.9% y-o-y, but the rate of decline has slowed from the 17.2% decline seen in the first quarter. In a number of countries, registrations in fact rose due to successful scrapping incentives schemes for old cars. In Germany, for instance, car registrations were up by nearly 40% y-o-y in May. Incentive schemes have now been introduced by 13 European countries: Austria, Cyprus, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Luxembourg, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Spain, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom. © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 8 of 12 Copper Monitor July 2009 www.crumonitor.com The USA is also planning to introduce a vehicle scrapping incentive plan. If implemented as proposed, the scheme would provide a grant of between $3,500-$4,500 per vehicle. The scheme could provide enough funding for around one million vehicle purchases. Both US and foreign vehicles could be eligible for the scheme. It will take some time, however, for improved sales to feed through to a significant recovery in car production. Although the rate of decline has slowed in Western Europe, with Q2 2009 car output looking set to be down by around 23% y-o-y to 2.7 million units, after a 34% y-o-y decline in Q1. In the USA, car production looks set to see a 43% y-o-y decline in Q2 after a 52% decline in Q1, with a worse outlook for commercial vehicles – down 57% in Q1 and 52% in Q2. Automobile production accounted for around 10% of European and North American copper demand (including scrap content) in 2008. ## **US wirerod production continues to decline** The latest ABMS data for May show a further weakening of US wirerod shipments, down 8% m-o-m and 25% y-o-y to 91,000t. In addition, inventories of both rod and raw materials increased in May, with cathode stocks reaching 21,000t and wirerod inventories hitting 34,000t, their highest level since October. s|e month|s, seas|onally| © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 9 of 12 Copper Monitor July 2009 **www.crumonitor.com** # Industry News ## **Production** - **Rio Tinto** has announced that it is to break off its potential US$19.5B deal with **Chinalco** , in favour of a US$15.2B rights issue, combined with a joint venture with rival **BHP Billiton** at their West Australian iron ore facilities. Originally the Chinalco deal would have involved Chinalco buying direct or indirect interest in several of Rio Tinto's mine properties, including part of its share of the **Escondida** copper mine in Chile, **Bingham Canyon** copper mine in the USA, part of its share of the **Grasberg** copper mine in Indonesia and the **La Granja** copper project in Peru. - On 21st June, **Xstrata** made a preliminary proposal to **Anglo American** for a transaction involving the group. The Board of Anglo American reviewed the proposal and said that it lacked strategic merit and the terms proposed were totally unacceptable. Press rumours and analysts reckon that Xstrata will start a hostile bid. If the merger occurs, the company would become the world’s largest copper mine producer (1,579,000t on a 2008 basis) and third largest copper refiner (1,033,000t on a 2008 basis). - In early June, a US bankruptcy court gave **Asarco** permission to set up custodial trust settlement agreements. These will allow payment to federal and state government of some US$275M regarding environmental claims for about 54 sites across the USA. **Grupo Mexico** has made a US$3.1B bid for Asarco, an increase over its previous bids of US$1.55B and US$2.9B. The latest Grupo offer includes US$1.46B in cash and the balance through a credit note. **Sterlite Resources** (a subsidiary of **Vedanta** ) increased its offer from US$1.7B to US$1.87B (US$1.1B in cash and a US$770M credit note) for Asarco. In addition, **Harbinger Capital** , who is a major bondholder in the Asarco bankruptcy case, has made a US$500M offer to take Asarco out of Chapter 11 and pay creditors. - **Konkola Copper Mines (KCM)** owned by **Vedanta Resources** has announced plans to more than double its copper output in 2009. KCM aims to produce 305,000t of copper cathode in 2009, up from approximately 140,000t in 2008. KCM also plans to re-start cobalt production in the medium term, with output capacity announced at 5,000t/y. No timeline for start-up has been announced. - On 11th June, **OZ Minerals’** shareholders approved the sale of most of its assets, excluding **Prominent Hill** and few others, to China’s **Minmetals** . Minmetals increased its offer by 15% a few hours before OZ Minerals’ meeting and paid a final amount of US$1,354M. - On 24th June, **Teck Metals** reported that based on geotechnical

issues it expects to reduce copper in concentrate production at its **Highland Valley** mine by 15.625t of copper in concentrate  (35Mlb) in H2 2009 and by 51,339t (115Mlb) in 2010.  Highland Valley is now expected to produce around 117,000t in 2009 compared to the original forecast of 130,000t. 

- **Inmet Mining** has announced it is to exchange its 18% equity interest in the **Ok Tedi** mine in Papua New Guinea for a 5% net smelter return royalty. The transaction has been designed to be neutral on a net asset basis. This will allow operator **Ok Tedi Mining** to pursue projects outside the scope of its current activities, which may require extra capital investment or temporarily reduce overall shareholder returns, without affecting Inmet Mining's financial returns from the current open pit mine. Ok Tedi mine is forecast to produce 161,000t of copper in concentrates in 2009 and continue operating until early in 2014. Ok Tedi Mining is reviewing the potential for a smaller underground operation following this.

- On 5<sup>th</sup> June, **Zambia** experienced blackouts throughout the country, including the Copperbelt, because a major distribution transformer on the national power grid was damaged by fire.  The country imports electricity from its neighbour DR Congo, but this is insufficient to allow mines to run at full capacity.  As a result, copper mines reduced their production.  It was reported that **Equinox Minerals** had to suspend operations at **Lumwana** for 18 hours. CRU expects Lumwana to produce 150,000t of copper in concentrate in 2009.  In addition, **Konkola Copper Mines (KCM)** had experienced a minor flood and it resumed operations two days later.  CRU expects KCM to produce 50,000t of copper in concentrate at its **Konkola** mine in 2009.  The blackout also affected **Mopani Copper Mines.** 

- On 22<sup>nd</sup> June, **PanAust** announced the failure of one of the two motors that drive the SAG mill at its **Phu Kham** operation in Laos.  In March, an identical ball mill motor failed and a spare motor was being used as a replacement.  The motor damaged in March is expected to be repaired and returned to site in early July.  PanAust anticipates that the process plant will be closed for between 11 and 23 days dependent on how quickly the motors can be repaired or the availability of identical ones.  In addition, PanAust has declared _force majeure_ on sales from Phu Kham.  CRU had estimated that Phu Kham would produce 65,000t of copper in concentrate in 2009. 

- On 3<sup>rd</sup> June, **Inmet Mining** announced that the first copper cathode was produced at its **Las Cruces** mine in Spain.  Las Cruces has a design capacity of 72,000t/y of copper cathode and is expected to produce 23,000t of copper cathode in 2009. 

## **Exploration and Development** 









- **Southern Copper Corporation (SCC)** has ann

ounced that it will move ahead with an expansion project of its **Toquepala** mine at Peru as the copper price has rebounded.  Earlier this year the project was put on hold.  The expansion would increase its milling capacity from 60,000t/d to 100,000t/d and works could start in mid-2010 depending on the result of the engineering studies.  In 2009, CRU expects Toquepala to produce 120,000t of copper in concentrates and 35,000t of copper cathode. 

- The desalination plant project for the expansion of the **Escondida** mine in Chile received environmental approval from the government. **BHP Billiton** , however, said this US$3.5B investment will be on hold as the company has frozen all growth expenditure. 

- **Rio Tinto** and **Codelco** signed an exploration agreement regarding the **Pasaca** prospect in northern Chile.  This is the fourth exploration agreement between the two companies. 

- **Codelco** and **Sociedad Punta del Cobre (Pucobre)** signed an exploration agreement over the **Puntillas – Galenosa** prospect, in Chile, which has a potential of 500Mt of mineral resources grading 0.25%Cu. 

## **Smelting and Refining** 



- On 18<sup>th</sup> June, **HudBay Minerals** announced that it expects to close its **Flin Flon** copper smelter in Manitoba (Canada) by July 2010.  Flin Flon produced 75,000t of copper blister in 2008 and CRU expects it to decline to 55,000t this year as it is no longer processing concentrates from third parties. As a result, HudBay Minerals’ **White Pine** refinery in Michigan (USA) is expected to close shortly after.  White Pine treats anode from Flin Flon and in 2009 it is expected to produce 55,000t of copper cathode.

## **Consumption** 











- Annual production capacity of flat rolled products in **South Korea** could exceed 300,000t in 2-3 years due to expansion projects at **Poongsan** and **Lee Ku Industrial** .  Total nominal capacity amounts to 260,000t but actual capacity is 240,000t.  Poongsan is focusing on high value-added products and intends to raise capacity by 23,000t by 2010.  The company is also starting a new coil centre in **Shenzhen, China** , that aims to ship 150-200t of rolled copper products per month, with the plan to raise that to 500t when the economy recovers.  Lee Ku is planning to install additional coldrolling facilities at its **Poseung** plant but the investment period has not been decided yet. 

- According to forecasts by **Aurubis** , **Europe’s** largest copper producer, copper demand in coming months will rebound.  A recovery in global economic growth will generate demand for copper, with **China** having a major role.  Aurubis anticipates that copper demand in China will rise by 8% in 2009.  As a result, global copper demand may experience a light increase despite the expected yearon-year contraction in other regions such as Europe.  The company antic

ipates that global copper demand in 2010 will grow by 2-5%. 

- A merchant from **Hebei Province, China** , started constructing a 120,000t copper wirerod and copper wire project in **Tongliao County, Inner Mongolia** .  Investment amounts to 100 million yuan (US$14.6 million) whilst the project will be put into production by the end of August 2009. 

- Industry data released by the **International Trade Commission** showed that **US** copper imports in April declined to 53,942t compared to 79,975t in March.  The construction and manufacturing sectors are still ailing despite some recent stability signs.  Copper imports in the short-term will continue to be challenged by the ongoing market uncertainty. 

- The **General Administration of Customs** reported that **Chinese** imports of refined copper and copper semis rose by 5.7% m-o-m to 422,666t in May.  That was significantly supported by restocking and reduced scrap availability, as well as arbitrage activity.  But demand from end-use sectors, such as home appliances manufacturers, slowed as end-users were reluctant to buy copper due to mixed signals on domestic consumption.
